fields.Father (prose): Moses Kranz, shoemaker in Kamienica Dolna
fields.Mother (prose): Hinde Turk
fields.Notes: Baracha, the illegitimate daughter of Hinde Turk, was born in Kamienica Dolna, Pilzno district, in the year 1899, that is, in the one-thousand-eight-hundred-and-ninety-ninth year. Paternity of this child was acknowledged by Moses Kranz, who entered into a lawful marriage with the child's mother in the year 1902 in Jaslo, recorded in the marriage register of the Israelite metrical district in Jaslo for the year 1902, Volume III, page 170/1, entry no. 26; therefore, the child was legitimated by the subsequent marriage of the parents and is legally entitled to bear the father's family name "Kranz." The entry was made pursuant to a rescript of the Voivodeship Office in Krakow dated 29 December 1931, reference SPD VI 1123/31, in Pilzno on 28 January 1932.

fields.Mother (prose): Hinde Kornhauser
fields.Notes: On the basis of a rescript of the High Imperial-Royal Governorship dated 14 September 1901, no. 95859, and an order of the Imperial-Royal District Office in Pilzno dated 24 September of the same year, no. 19861, the following is entered: Hinde Kornhauser gave birth in Skurowa, in the month of January of the year one thousand eight hundred seventy-three (1873), to an illegitimate daughter, who at the time of blessing was given the name "Hannah". Note of the registrar. According to the above order, this additional immatriculation entry is to be made in 1873 of the book of births but it was not possible to enter this in 1873 because there was no space. Therefore it was placed here under current serial number and a report given to the district.

translator_note: Blima Kichel's birth is not listed in the books of Brzostek. Her existence and her parents are inferred from US immigration records. 17 Sep 1920 aboard SS Aquitania to Ellis Island, Blima Kichel age 25 single female tailor, listed father Leiser Kichel in Brzostek as next of kin. Age 25 in Sep 1920 → born ~Sep 1894 to Sep 1895. Joseph Kichel (b-1895-25, 22 Aug 1895) was confirmed same family and also emigrated (SS Hamburg 5 Feb 1914). It is assumed that Blima and Joseph were siblings but cannot both be born in 1895 by natural gestation — Blima likely b.late 1894 (older sister) or born in Biecz/Rzepiennik before the family settled in Brzostek (Leiser from Rzepiennik Strzyżewski, Esther from Biecz per m-1896-2)

translator_note: Groom written 'Józef Langer false Herman', 'illegitimate son'. He was born 17 May 1895 (b-1895-13) before his parents' civil marriage of 27 Jun 1907 (m-1907-5), which under Austrian law legitimated an acknowledged child; his birth entry carries no legitimation note, so the clerk may have copied 'illegitimate' from it. Elsewhere the clerks put the legal surname first and the used one after "false" (e.g. "Israel Hirsch Rieger, falsely Löw", b-1912-17; "Chaim Tyder false Horowitz", m-1910-8). By that order this would be "Herman false Langer": legally Herman after his mother, called Langer after his father. The names appear to be inverted here. The text is kept as written.
